title: Stalk vanishing for one scalar cone
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let D(\mathcal O_X) be its derived category [def-pc-derived-category], and let g be a compatible family of local sections of \mathcal O_X [def-sc-derived-global-scalar]. Let E\xrightarrow{g}E\to K\to E[1] be a distinguished triangle. If x\in X belongs to D(g(X)), or if H^n(E)_x=0 for every integer n, then H^n(K)_x=0 for every integer n. Here vanishing means that the underlying additive stalk is a subsingleton.

source.place: Tag 08EK (Lemma 36.13.10), cone construction; triangulated consequences in Tags 05QR, 05QS, 05QT

proof.text: For T the given distinguished scalar triangle, Mathlib DerivedCategory.HomologySequence.exact₃ gives the exact short complex H^n(E) → H^n(K) → H^(n+1)(E). Apply clause (5) of module_stalk_exact [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] to obtain its exact stalk short complex. This uses homology sheaves directly; no derived stalk functor or comparison with stalk complexes is constructed.

Prove in Lean that homology is linear over compatible global sections [def-sc-derived-global-scalar]. The short-complex functor is linear componentwise; compose it with Mathlib ShortComplex.homologyFunctor_linear and descend through DerivedCategory.Q using Localization.functor_linear_iff and homologyFunctorFactors. For a sheaf module, represent any stalk element by a germ on U. stalkFunctor_map_germ_apply and PresheafOfModules.germ_smul identify the stalk scalar action with the germ of g_U. The restriction equation for the compatible family and germ_res_apply identify this scalar germ with the germ of g_top.

In the basic-open case, Scheme.mem_basicOpen_top identifies the top-section germ as a unit. IsUnit.smul_bijective and ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective show the scalar maps on homology stalks in degrees n and n+1 are isomorphisms. Map the triangle zero composite and HomologySequence.δ_comp through the stalk functor; cancel the degree-n epimorphism and degree-(n+1) monomorphism to show both maps of the exact stalk complex are zero. ShortComplex.Exact.isZero_X₂ then makes its middle module zero.

In the input-acyclic case, ModuleCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton makes the degree-n and degree-(n+1) input stalk modules zero. IsZero.eq_of_src and IsZero.eq_of_tgt give zero incoming and outgoing maps. Apply ShortComplex.Exact.isZero_X₂ to the exact stalk short complex, then ModuleCat.subsingleton_of_isZero to finish both cases in every degree.

lean.statement: theorem scalar_cone_stalk_vanishing (X : Scheme.{u}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))] (g : RingCat.sectionsSubring (X.sheaf.obj ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat.{u})) (E K : schemeDerivedCategory X) (b : E ⟶ K) (d : K ⟶ E⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧) (hcone : Triangle.mk (schemeDerivedScalar X g (𝟙 E)) b d ∈ distTriang (schemeDerivedCategory X)) (x : X) (hx : x ∈ X.basicOpen (g.val (op ⊤)) ∨ ∀ n : ℤ, Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj E).val.presheaf x))) : ∀ n : ℤ, Subsingleton (↑(TopCat.Presheaf.stalk ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj K).val.presheaf x))
